Subject: Redwood DPA & breach notification timeline

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick demo this week. Procurement asked me to circle back on two items so we can get legal to finalize the DPA:

1) Signature method: we prefer DocuSign but can accept AdobeSign. Can you send the executable link once Redwood's legal approves the final redline?

2) Breach notification timing: our security team expects initial customer notification within 24 hours for incidents that materially affect customer data. We understand industry norms are often 72 hours (GDPR). Can Redwood accommodate a 24-hour initial notice commitment, with a technical follow-up and remediation timeline to be agreed?

Attached is our standard DPA template (we'll upload into DocuSign once countersigned). Let me know if you need anything from procurement to speed approvals.

Best,
Sarah Liu
Senior Counsel, FinBank

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 10:23:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Redwood DPA & breach notification timeline

Team / Sarah —

I reviewed FinBank's template and the 24-hour initial notice ask. Proposed approach (high level):

- Operational compromise: Redwood can commit to "initial acknowledgment" to the customer within 24 hours of confirmation that an event impacting customer data has occurred, limited to a high-level status (we have identified an incident / we are investigating; anticipated impact unknown).

- Material breach definition: Keep the materiality threshold tied to the law/regulatory definition (GDPR/State breach laws). For incidents that meet the material breach definition, Redwood will provide a substantive incident report within 72 hours of detection (unless constrained by active investigation).

- Cooperation & evidence: Add clear cooperation language — Redwood will provide forensic artifacts, logs, and a post-incident remediation plan upon request, subject to reasonable protections (redactions for internal-only data, protective order for shared raw logs).

- Subprocessors & notif: We will notify customers of impacted subprocessors within the same timeline and maintain a current subprocessor inventory. We cannot pre-authorize ad-hoc subprocessor replacements without notice.

I've attached a redline (DPA_Redline_v3.docx) with suggested edits that - preserves our standard limits (investigation window, non-public internal details), - offers the 24-hour acknowledgement language FinBank wants, and - restates cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs + Data Privacy Framework where applicable).

If Procurement/Legal at FinBank are comfortable with the acknowledgement + 72-hour substantive report compromise, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DPA_Redline_v3.docx; Subprocessor_Inventory_20260220.csv]

Mina — thanks for the helpful redline and the compromise language. Procurement is ok with acknowledgement + 72-hour substantive report as long as:

- The 24-hour acknowledgement explicitly covers notification to the customer's security operations center (SOC) and includes channel and contact info.
- There is an escalation contact (phone + email) available 24/7 for severity "P1" incidents.
- DocuSign envelope is provided with the redline attached so our legal team can see final language in the executed doc.

Can you add the SOC contact clause and confirm we can include Tim at DocuSign to generate a signature envelope? If so, procurement will schedule execution next week.

Sarah
